title: Braden Scale (Pressure Injury Risk)
keywords: 6 subscales, 5 scored 1-4 and friction-shear scored 1-3, total range 6-23
lower score means higher risk, opposite direction from most scores
17 or higher no measurable risk, 15-16 low, 13-14 moderate, 10-12 high, 9 or below very high
sources: Bergstrom N, Braden BJ, Laguzza A, Holman V. The Braden Scale for Predicting Pressure Sore Risk. Nurs Res. 1987;36(4):205-210.
Risk-band cutoffs (≥17 no risk / 15-16 low / 13-14 moderate / 10-12 high / ≤9 very high) WebSearch-verified against contemporary nursing-assessment references.

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap (Content audit 2026-09-14, Batch 4). Subscale descriptor wording follows standard clinical phrasing rather than the copyrighted original instrument's exact text; point values and structure (6 subscales, 5 scored 1-4, friction/shear scored 1-3, total 6-23) verified.

purpose: Standardized bedside assessment of pressure-injury risk in a hospitalized patient, driving how aggressively to intervene (repositioning frequency, support surface, nutrition consult) — note the score runs the OPPOSITE direction from most clinical scores: LOWER means HIGHER risk.
notes: Unlike most scores in this app, a LOWER Braden total means HIGHER risk — double check you're reading the direction correctly before acting on it.

items.label: Sensory perception — ability to respond meaningfully to pressure-related discomfort

options.label: Completely limited — unresponsive to painful stimuli, or limited ability to feel pain over most of the body

Very limited — responds only to painful stimuli; cannot communicate discomfort except by moaning/restlessness, or has a sensory impairment limiting the ability to feel pain/discomfort over half the body
Slightly limited — responds to verbal commands but cannot always communicate discomfort, or has some sensory impairment limiting ability to feel pain/discomfort in 1-2 extremities
No impairment — responds to verbal commands, no sensory deficit that would limit ability to feel/voice pain or discomfort

items.label: Moisture — degree to which skin is exposed to moisture

options.label: Constantly moist — skin kept moist almost constantly by sweat, urine, etc.; dampness detected every time patient is moved
Very moist — skin often but not always moist; linen must be changed at least once per shift
Occasionally moist — skin occasionally moist, requiring an extra linen change about once a day
Rarely moist — skin usually dry, linen changed only at routine intervals
Bedfast — confined to bed
Chairfast — ability to walk severely limited or nonexistent; cannot bear own weight/must be assisted into a chair or wheelchair
Walks occasionally — walks occasionally during the day but for very short distances, with or without assistance; spends majority of each shift in bed/chair
Walks frequently — walks outside the room at least twice a day and inside the room at least once every 2 hours during waking hours

items.label: Mobility — ability to change and control body position

options.label: Completely immobile — cannot make even slight changes in body/extremity position without assistance
Very limited — makes occasional slight changes in body/extremity position but cannot make frequent or significant changes independently
Slightly limited — makes frequent, though slight, changes in body/extremity position independently
No limitation — makes major and frequent changes in position without assistance
Very poor — never eats a complete meal, rarely eats more than a third of any food offered, eats poorly overall, or is NPO/on clear liquids/IV fluids for more than 5 days
Probably inadequate — rarely eats a complete meal, generally eats only about half of food offered; occasionally takes a supplement, or receives less than optimal tube-feed/TPN volume
Adequate — eats over half of most meals, occasionally refuses a meal but will usually take a supplement if offered, or is on tube feeding/TPN meeting most nutritional needs
Excellent — eats most of every meal, never refuses a meal, does not require supplementation

Problem — requires moderate to maximum assistance to move; complete lifting without sliding against sheets is impossible; frequent sliding down in bed/chair requiring frequent repositioning with maximum assistance; spasticity/contractures/agitation lead to almost constant friction

Potential problem — moves feebly or requires minimum assistance; during a move, skin probably slides to some extent against sheets/chair/restraints; maintains relatively good position in chair/bed most of the time but occasionally slides down
No apparent problem — moves independently in bed/chair with sufficient strength to lift up completely during a move; maintains good position at all times

interpretation.label: 17-23 — no measurable risk
interpretation.detail: Continue routine skin assessment and standard preventive practice.

interpretation.label: 15-16 — low risk
interpretation.detail: Basic preventive measures: routine repositioning schedule, moisture management, nutrition attention.

interpretation.label: 13-14 — moderate risk
interpretation.detail: Escalate: more frequent repositioning, a pressure-redistribution support surface, closer skin checks.

interpretation.label: 10-12 — high risk
interpretation.detail: Aggressive prevention: frequent repositioning, specialty support surface, nutrition consult, heel protection.

interpretation.label: ≤ 9 — very high risk
interpretation.detail: Maximal prevention effort and close, frequent skin surveillance — this patient is at substantial risk without it.

buildNote: engine: additive, 6 subscales summing to 6-23. Subscale wording is a faithful paraphrase of the standard clinical descriptors rather than the original copyrighted instrument's exact phrasing.
